notes:
I don't have any notes for you yet. My first attempt to read the sources failed straight away: the research tool said I had no calls left before any page loaded. So I haven't read a single page on Job 28.

You asked me to report only what the pages say, give a URL for every point and not fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I have no source text, I'd be writing from memory and attaching URLs I haven't checked, so I've left the commentary out rather than do that.

When the tool is working again, these are the pages I'd read first:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** Enduring Word on Job 28 (enduringword.com/bible-commentary/job-28/), and the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages for Job 28 on biblehub.com (for example biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/job/28.htm), plus Precept Austin's Job 28 page.
- **Modern scholarship:** the NET Bible notes on Job 28 (netbible.org), which deal with the hard Hebrew in verses 1–11 and the gemstone names in verses 16–19. I'd also search Bible Odyssey for whether this chapter is the narrator speaking or Job.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** searches on Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, Spurgeon.org, Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), the LCMS and 1517 for Job 28 and verse 28, "the fear of the Lord is wisdom."
- **Catholic and Orthodox readings:** searches on New Advent (including the Church Fathers on Job), Catholic.com and OCA.org.
- **Popular modern teaching:** I'd check whether any allowed site links verses 1–19 (mining and wealth) with prosperity teaching. I'd include it only if a page actually makes that link.

Ask again and I'll work through this list and write the notes verse by verse with a URL on every point, leaving out anything I can't find.
